feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/analytics depth. It reads professionally, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, culminating in leadership roles with strong evidence of increasing responsibility.  
- Good credibility through concrete scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, analytics stack).  
- Strong alignment between headline, summary, skills, and experience in digital strategy, web modernization, and cross-channel communications.

1. Top improvements  
- Tighten and de-duplicate: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and save space.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements beyond responsibilities, especially in the freelance role and earlier positions (e.g., growth, efficiency gains, engagement improvements).  
- Fix writing/style consistency: use “12 years of experience” (not “12 years experience”); add the serial comma consistently (“web, email, social, and multimedia”); standardize punctuation/hyphenation across bullets (“organization-wide,” “front-end,” “member-facing”). No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership profile. It would be stronger with sharper positioning, one or two concrete differentiators, and slightly less overlap with the competencies section.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Lead with your seniority and niche: digital strategy, platform modernization, and mission-driven/public-sector communications.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with tighter, higher-impact wording such as “multi-channel digital communications.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving multi-channel communications, web modernization, and content operations for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, editorial workflow design, and digital systems that improve coordination, governance, and audience engagement. Strong background in advocacy and public-sector messaging, with a proven ability to translate complex technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language repeat heavily in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” is already reinforced throughout the NACo experience section.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it feel more strategic and less repetitive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level language: “Digital strategy & transformation” → “Enterprise digital strategy,” “Multi-channel communication” → “Cross-channel communications leadership.”
- Reduce overlap with technical sections by keeping this block capability-focused, not tool-focused.
- Improve parallel structure and consistency: use plural nouns or noun phrases throughout.
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise digital strategy • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform governance & CMS administration • Editorial systems & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Digital operations & systems architecture • Stakeholder and cross-functional coordination • Advocacy, policy & public-sector communications • Multimedia, livestream and event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- “Data analytics & reporting” and “Web & CMS administration” overlap with Topline Skills and Technical + IT.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around outcomes, leadership, and the few contributions that best differentiate it from the NACo roles below.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + client type: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 sharper points, e.g.:
- “Built cross-functional digital workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Delivered front-end/CMS implementation and troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.”
- “Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval strategy, structured content design, and user discovery.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages, users, teams supported, launch dates, efficiency gains, engagement lifts, or reduced publishing time.
- Replace “Support/Advise/Deliver” with stronger verbs: lead, build, design, launch, streamline.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Governance, analytics, and Drupal modernization overlap with the NACo Director role; emphasize consulting ownership, AI search, and campaign builds here.
- The microsite/search work also appears in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management themes already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into sharper outcome-led bullets: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more specific or results-based: add email list size, engagement growth, campaign performance, or follower growth if available; otherwise shorten this bullet.
- Tighten operations language: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio and expanded analytics/reporting across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving production capacity and leadership reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version higher-level and more strategic.
- Video/programming language also appears in older NACo roles; emphasize studio build-out and enterprise capability here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the earlier NACo role and the later Director role. Make it more clearly about operational leadership, editorial systems, and channel growth at the manager-to-director transition point.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and progression: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging organization-wide.”
- Tighten bullets and start with outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and distinct: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems bullet: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” appears in the 2015–2018 role; avoid repeating that exact phrasing.
- “publishing workflows/governance” overlaps with the 2022–2024 role; keep this version focused on execution rather than enterprise leadership.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and distinct strengths not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, higher-signal wording tied to recent work:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms
- Editorial governance and content operations design
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Advocacy and member-facing messaging strategy
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for “Campaign and storytelling architecture” or “User-centered content strategy” to sound more senior and differentiated.
- If space allows, add one scale cue from recent roles, e.g., “10,000+ page web ecosystems” or “50+ publisher environments.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” repeat Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with multiple NACo roles; keep only if paired with a more distinctive leadership angle.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a generic tool dump and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize current, differentiating strengths tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Drupal and CMS modernization” instead of listing multiple platforms first.
- Tighten and prioritize recent strengths: Drupal, CMS modernization, front-end implementation, API/workflow integration, AI-enabled search.
- Consider: “Drupal & CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • SharePoint, WordPress & Power Pages • AI-enabled search experiences”
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “AI-enabled search experiences” → “AI-enabled search and structured content discovery”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and save full platform/tool lists for Technical + IT.
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase if possible.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” To earn its place as a topline skill block, it should emphasize decision-making and business impact, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing: “Analytics strategy, KPI framework design, executive reporting, user behavior analysis, SEO/performance optimization.”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Tighten wording and group related items: “KPI design & dashboarding” instead of separate “KPI design” and “Leadership reporting.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & KPI design • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO, UX and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating the full tool stack elsewhere unless this section is positioned as a concise, impact-oriented summary.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skills item is relevant, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and older NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production capability and recent/most credible strengths rather than listing basic tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as outcome-oriented capabilities, e.g.:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- In-house studio buildout and operations
- PTZ/multi-camera production workflows
- Consider changing “Event Delivery” to “Event Production” for stronger industry phrasing.
- Drop “video production and editing” in favor of “broadcast-quality video production and post-production” to sound more senior.
- If space allows, align with proven experience: “studio operations” → “studio buildout and operations,” reflecting the NACo achievement.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This partially duplicates “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies.
- Avoid repeating detailed livestream/video language elsewhere unless tied to a measurable accomplishment.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use this space to signal depth and recency, especially around Drupal, which is clearly the strongest and most current platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add proficiency/context, e.g. **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites, governance) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, make Drupal version-specific for credibility: **Drupal 10/9**
- Consider trimming lower-signal items if not used recently: **Drupal 10/9 • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills item “Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms plus modernization context.
- “GitHub Pages” may undersell seniority unless tied to a meaningful use case; consider removing if it was only occasional.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this item reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current, implementation-focused, and aligned to the recent Drupal/analytics/automation work shown in experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Replace with: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- If space allows, sharpen for relevance: Front-end development (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations • Tag management (Google Tag Manager) • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • CI/CD and deployment automation (GitHub Actions)
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) if you want a more senior tone: HTML • CSS • JavaScript • jQuery

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere; avoid adding it here unless replacing a less specific item.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation”/“Airtable systems” already highlighted elsewhere. Make it more purposeful by grouping tools around automation and operational coordination.

Suggested edit:
- Retitle to emphasize function: “Workflow Automation & Team Operations” or “Automation, PM & Collaboration Tools.”
- Reorder by relevance/recency: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier first; then Jira/Asana; then Slack/Teams; Trello/Basecamp last or remove if less current.
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams”  
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of more tools: “Airtable (workflow systems), Power Automate/Zapier (process automation), Jira/Asana (project operations).”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills, so avoid repeating the same language here.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; if space is tight, they add less differentiation than automation platforms.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools for this profile, but the line is too bare and undersells email/engagement leadership shown in recent NACo roles. It would be stronger if framed around platform administration and campaign operations, not just vendor names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, strengthen with scope: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Newsletter operations • Audience segmentation • Campaign deployment
- Best option if you have hands-on ownership: Administered and used Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys, Higher Logic and Mailchimp for newsletter publishing, audience segmentation and campaign delivery

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding broad “email strategy” language here; that is already covered in Work Experience and Core Competencies.
- If Dynamics 365 use was limited, don’t overstate ownership—keep this as a tools list rather than an accomplishment statement.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads as setup rather than impact. Tighten it to emphasize team-building, channel ownership, and concrete outputs without repeating achievements already covered in later NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground scope and advancement: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and support daily operations across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add clearer contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, improved cross-channel publishing workflows, and produced recurring digital content including livestreams and weekly video updates.”
- Make management more precise: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised day-to-day work of a digital media associate.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, publishing volume, or workflow/time savings.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the later “weekly advocacy video update”; differentiate this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow/governance language already used more strongly in 2018–2024 roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads generically and underplays impact. Since later NACo roles already cover digital leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation/research support and the “first podcast” milestone.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground scope and firsts: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Tighten the digital sentence and make the podcast the anchor achievement: “Produced digital and multimedia content, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If you can, add outputs or reach: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, stakeholders/program teams served, or content pieces produced.
- Consider a 2-bullet format for clarity rather than one paragraph.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid broad phrases like “digital content production and multimedia materials,” which overlap with later Digital Media Manager/Producer and Associate Communications Director entries.
- Don’t overstate leadership here; save team-building/operations language for the more senior NACo roles.
